title_en: Mo Xuerong's Application for State Compensation
ruling_gist_en: In criminal compensation cases where criminal and civil legal relationships are intertwined, to examine the legality of the seizure and recovery actions by public security organs, on the one hand, the binding effect of the factual findings and the operative part of effective criminal and civil judgments on criminal compensation cases should be adhered to; on the other hand, through comprehensive review and judgment of the existing evidence, the facts not addressed in the effective criminal and civil legal documents should be accurately determined in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Mo Xuerong's Application for State Compensation Case

[Ruling Summary]

In criminal compensation cases where criminal and civil legal relations are intertwined, when reviewing whether the seizure and recovery actions of a public security organ are lawful, one must, on the one hand, adhere to the binding effect of the factual findings and operative parts of effective criminal and civil judgments on the criminal compensation case, and on the other hand, through comprehensive review and evaluation of the available evidence, accurately determine the facts not addressed in the effective criminal and civil legal documents in accordance with the law.

Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court

State Compensation Decision

(2012) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 3

Claimant for Compensation: Mo Xuerong, male, born on December 19, 1952, Han ethnicity, resident identity card number 440104195212192215, residing at Room 606, No. 127 Yingyuan Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Hu Linli, lawyer of Guangdong Baike Law Firm.

Respondent (Obligor for Compensation): Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department. Address: No. 97 Huanghua Road, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Chunsheng, Director of the Department.

Agent ad litem: Ren Zechao, Cadre of the Economic Crime Investigation Bureau of the Department.

Agent ad litem: Guo Jinan, Cadre of the Legal Affairs Division of the Department.

Reconsideration Authority: Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China. Address: No. 14 East Chang'an Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing City.

Legal Representative: Guo Shengkun, Minister of the Ministry.

Agent ad litem: Wang Guowu, Cadre of the Legal Affairs Bureau of the Ministry.

Agent ad litem: Li Qianqian, Cadre of the Legal Affairs Bureau of the Ministry.

The Claimant for Compensation, Mo Xuerong, applied to the Compensation Committee of this Court for a compensation decision regarding his application for compensation for criminal illegal seizure and recovery by the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department, being dissatisfied with the criminal compensation decision of the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department, Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1, and the criminal compensation reconsideration decision of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Ministry of Public Security), Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1. The Compensation Committee of this Court has lawfully tried this case, and the trial is now concluded.

Mo Xuerong's Application: The Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department seized RMB 4,040,000 from him and has not yet processed it. The effective criminal judgment did not find this amount to be stolen money, nor did it find it to be property of the Business Department of the Guangdong Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department); the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department's lawsuit for return of the seized funds was dismissed, and it has not reasserted its rights thereafter; therefore, the RMB 4,040,000 is Mo Xuerong's lawful property. The Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration determination that Tianlong Company borrowed RMB 2,100,000 from Beijing Huayin Gold and Silver Jewelry Company (hereinafter referred to as Huayin Company) and Zhongyin Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhongyin Company) under the People's Bank of China through Qingyuan Xuanming Industry and Trade Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xuanming Company), repaid principal of RMB 3,800,000, and offset the principal with the interest of RMB 1,080,000 paid by Tianlong Company to Beijing Dongcheng Huayue Industrial Company (hereinafter referred to as Huayue Company) lacks a factual basis. The amounts of RMB 6,934,562.5 and RMB 849,000 that Cao Huixiong repaid to Guangzhou Saiche Association and Guangzhou Sanlian Overseas Chinese Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanlian Company) respectively, which the Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration did not recognize as funds repaid by Mo Xuerong for his borrowing, are inconsistent with the facts. During the trial by the Compensation Committee of this Court, Mo Xuerong supplemented his application, stating that the effective criminal judgment found that Tianlong Company borrowed funds from Cao Huixiong, but the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department seized Mo Xuerong's personal property of RMB 4,040,000, which constitutes an error in the subject of enforcement. Therefore, he requests the revocation of the Ministry of Public Security's criminal compensation reconsideration decision, Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1, and orders the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department to return the seized RMB 4,040,000 to Mo Xuerong along with interest of RMB 4,200,000.

Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department's Defense: During the investigation, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department seized the RMB 4,040,000 voluntarily surrendered by Mo Xuerong as ill-gotten gains, which complies with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law. Moreover, the effective criminal judgment has admitted the seizure list as evidence and deducted this amount when calculating the actual losses of the victims. Mo Xuerong's claim that this RMB 4,040,000 is his lawful property is untenable. Mo Xuerong borrowed RMB 13,040,000, repaid RMB 8,480,000, surrendered ill-gotten gains of RMB 4,040,000, and still owes RMB 520,000. The RMB 6,934,562.5 and RMB 849,000 that Mo Xuerong claims to have repaid are, respectively, the compensation settlement for the cooperative real estate project between Tianlong Company and Jinfeng Company, a subsidiary of the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department, and Cao Huixiong's loan from Mo Xuerong's Guangdong New Generation Computer City, not the borrowing funds repaid by Mo Xuerong. Therefore, it requests that the criminal compensation decision of the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department, Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1, be sustained.

The Ministry of Public Security agreed with the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department's defense and further stated: The Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department has already advanced the principal and interest for all unpaid deposit certificates, and the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Intermediate Court) dismissed the department's lawsuit on the ground that it was not within the scope of criminal incidental civil actions, without conducting a substantive trial on its claim. Therefore, Mo Xuerong's argument that the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department is not a victim is untenable. The Ministry of Public Security's criminal compensation reconsideration decision, Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1, should be sustained.

The Compensation Committee of this Court finds through trial:

During the investigation of the suspected crimes of Cao Huixiong, former manager of Jinfeng Company; Zhang Tao, former deputy manager of the Xihua Road Sub-branch of the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department; and Zhao Leiyuan, accountant of the Real Estate Management Service Center of Guangdong Great Wall Construction General Company, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department, based on the flow of the involved funds, interrogated Mo Xuerong on July 30, 1996. Mo Xuerong voluntarily offered to surrender ill-gotten gains. From August 5 to December 19, 1996, Mo Xuerong surrendered ill-gotten gains five times, totaling RMB 4,040,000. The Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department issued receipts and produced a seizure list. During the case investigation, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department seized and froze a total of RMB 8,675,449.37 in involved funds, including this RMB 4,040,000, and the seizure list was transferred with the case. On February 27, 2001, the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rendered the criminal judgment (1999) Sui Zhong Xing Jing Chu Zi No. 68, finding that Cao Huixiong and Zhang Tao (separately handled), with the assistance of Zhao Leiyuan, illegally borrowed and used client funds by attracting deposits at high interest rates and issuing bank time deposit certificates without recording them in the bank's accounts. The amount of illegally borrowed funds not yet repaid at the time of the case was RMB 20,021,400. After deducting the funds recovered by the public security organs, RMB 8,675,449.37, the actual economic loss suffered by the victims was RMB 11,345,950.63. The court accordingly convicted Cao Huixiong and Zhao Leiyuan of the crime of illegally borrowing funds with off-book client funds, sentencing Cao Huixiong to twelve years' imprisonment and Zhao Leiyuan to six years' imprisonment. After the judgment was pronounced, Cao Huixiong and Zhao Leiyuan did not appeal, and the prosecutorial authority did not protest. The judgment has become legally effective.

According to the above effective criminal judgment, from May 1994 to August 1995, Tianlong Company, operated by Mo Xuerong, borrowed funds through Cao Huixiong and Zhang Tao five times, totaling RMB 13,040,000, and repaid principal of RMB 7,400,000 and interest and spreads of RMB 2,936,594. The specific facts are as follows:

On May 12, 1994, upon Mo Xuerong's contact with Yinxing Company of Dongshan District, Guangzhou City (hereinafter referred to as Yinxing Company), Cao Huixiong and Zhang Tao transferred RMB 1,000,000 from Yinxing Company into an account of Xuanming Company, a private enterprise operated by Zhang Tao's younger brother Zhang Wensheng, and then into the account of Tianlong Company. Zhang Tao issued to Yinxing Company a six-month time deposit certificate from the Xihua Road Sub-branch of the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department. On October 25 of the same year, Tianlong Company repaid Yinxing Company principal of RMB 1,000,000 and interest and spreads of RMB 116,900, totaling RMB 1,116,900.

In May 1994, upon contact by Mo Xuerong, Cao Huixiong, and Zhang Tao, representatives of Huayin Company, Zhongyin Company, and Huayue Company came to Guangzhou from Beijing to make high-interest deposits. On May 16, 1994, Cao Huixiong and Zhang Tao transferred draft funds of RMB 3,800,000 from Huayin Company and Zhongyin Company into the account of Xuanming Company, of which RMB 2,100,000 was then transferred into the account of Tianlong Company; they transferred RMB 5,000,000 from Huayue Company into the account of Xuanming Company, of which RMB 4,340,000 was then transferred into the account of Tianlong Company; and they issued one-year time deposit certificates from the Xihua Road Sub-branch of the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department to Huayin Company, Zhongyin Company, and Huayue Company respectively. Upon maturity, Tianlong Company, upon arrangement by Cao Huixiong, issued three draft orders for amounts of RMB 1,664,700, RMB 255,254, and RMB 2,940,970 respectively, directly repaying principal of RMB 3,800,000 to Huayin Company and Zhongyin Company, along with interest and spreads of RMB 1,060,924, totaling RMB 4,860,924. The RMB 5,000,000 from Huayue Company was renewed upon maturity. Tianlong Company, upon arrangement by Cao Huixiong, successively paid Huayue Company the matured interest of RMB 549,000 and renewal spreads of RMB 531,000, totaling RMB 1,080,000. This RMB 1,080,000 was later confirmed by the effective civil mediation document (1999) Dong Fa Jing Chu Zi No. 361 as having been offset against the principal lent by Huayue Company.

On June 22, 1994, Cao Huixiong and Zhang Tao again arranged a high-interest deposit for Huayin Company, directly transferring RMB 2,600,000 of that company into the account of Tianlong Company, and Zhang Tao issued to Huayin Company a one-year time deposit certificate from the Xihua Road Sub-branch of the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department. Tianlong Company later repaid Huayin Company principal of RMB 2,600,000 and interest and spreads of RMB 678,770, totaling RMB 3,278,770.

On August 29, 1995, Cao Huixiong contacted Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine to arrange a high-interest deposit. Cao Huixiong and Zhang Tao directly transferred RMB 3,000,000 of the hospital's RMB 5,000,000 in lent funds into the account of Tianlong Company, and Zhang Tao issued to the hospital a one-year time deposit certificate from the Xihua Road Sub-branch of the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department. By the time Cao Huixiong's case was discovered, Tianlong Company had not yet repaid the principal and interest to the hospital.

Another fact found:

(1) Tianlong Company was established in 1993. Mo Xuerong and his wife Lai Lili contributed 60% and 20% of the capital respectively. Mo Xuerong served as the legal representative. The company did not register for tax purposes. During the investigation of Cao Huixiong's suspected criminal case, Mo Xuerong stated to the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department that Tianlong Company was a private enterprise operated by him. During the trial of this case, Mo Xuerong also admitted this to the Compensation Committee of this Court.

Guangdong New Generation Computer City Co., Ltd. was established in 1995, with Mo Xuerong as its legal representative. The company was dissolved in 2003.

(2) In March 1994, Jinfeng Company jointly developed the comprehensive commercial and residential building project at Fujin Road, Dongshan District, Guangzhou City, with Guangzhou Yuexiu District Xiangxing Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Xiangxing Company). Jinfeng Company invested RMB 3,867,200 through Xuanming Company. On June 3, 1994, Tianlong Company signed an agreement with Xiangxing Company and Jinfeng Company to join the project. In February 1995, Xiangxing Company withdrew. Tianlong Company and Jinfeng Company transferred the project to the Qingyuan Sales Office of Guangdong Securities Company for RMB 22,000,000. On March 22 of the same year, Tianlong Company paid Jinfeng Company RMB 6,934,562.5 from the project transfer proceeds, of which RMB 5,787,500 was paid as principal and interest under the original investment agreement, and an additional RMB 1,147,062.5 was paid at Cao Huixiong's request. Cao Huixiong used this RMB 6,934,562.5 to repay borrowed funds to Guangzhou Saiche Association. On October 25, 1995, Cao Huixiong entrusted his elder brother Cao Huisong to borrow RMB 849,000 from Guangdong New Generation Computer City to repay borrowed funds to Sanlian Company. Cao Huixiong noted this fact on the receipt collected by Cao Huisong, which was extracted by the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department on April 2, 1998, acknowledging this fact. Whether these RMB 6,934,562.5 and RMB 849,000 were borrowed funds repaid by Tianlong Company was not addressed in the effective criminal judgment (1999) Sui Zhong Xing Jing Chu Zi No. 68. Mo Xuerong provided to the Compensation Committee of this Court a written testimony by Cao Huixiong dated May 8, 2012, to prove that both sums were borrowed funds repaid by Tianlong Company; and a written testimony by Lai Lili dated the 10th of the same month, proving that Lai Lili handed over Tianlong Company's check for RMB 6,934,562.5 to Cao Huixiong.

(3) From December 1998 to December 2005, the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department, due to deposit dispute lawsuits filed by the Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Huayue Company, and other lenders of funds in the illegal borrowing case involving Cao Huixiong, successively paid a total of RMB 26,112,709.55 in principal and interest for uncashed deposit certificates. During the trial of Cao Huixiong's illegal borrowing case, the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department filed an incidental civil action. Both the Guangzhou Intermediate Court and the Guangdong High People's Court dismissed the action on the ground that it was not within the scope of criminal incidental civil actions. Thereafter, the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department (later renamed China Agricultural Bank Guangzhou Taojin Sub-branch) repeatedly applied in writing to the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department for the return of the seized and frozen funds. During the trial by the Compensation Committee of this Court, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department decided to return the seized and frozen funds of RMB 8,675,449.37 from Cao Huixiong's illegal borrowing case to China Agricultural Bank Guangzhou Taojin Sub-branch. This sub-branch has fully received the seized principal of RMB 4,240,000 (including Mo Xuerong's RMB 4,040,000) and the frozen funds and interest of RMB 4,672,132.96, totaling RMB 8,912,132.96.

On December 14, 2011, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department received Mo Xuerong's application for criminal compensation. Mo Xuerong requested confirmation that the department's seizure of his property was unlawful, and the return of the seized RMB 4,040,000 and interest of RMB 4,200,000 (calculated at the bank's time deposit rate from August 12, 1996, to December 31, 2011). The Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department found: The department deposited the ill-gotten gains of RMB 4,040,000 surrendered by Mo Xuerong into a dedicated account, issued receipts, and transferred the seizure list with the case. Its seizure action was lawful. The effective criminal judgment admitted the seizure list, confirmed that this RMB 4,040,000 was funds recovered after the case was discovered, and deducted it when determining the actual losses. Mo Xuerong's claim that this RMB 4,040,000 was unrelated to the criminal case was untenable. Therefore, on February 8, 2012, it issued the criminal compensation decision Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1, denying compensation to Mo Xuerong.

Mo Xuerong was dissatisfied and applied to the Ministry of Public Security for reconsideration. The Ministry of Public Security found: The involved funds voluntarily returned by Mo Xuerong have been determined by the effective criminal judgment to be ill-gotten gains. The seizure action of the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department was in compliance with the law. Existing evidence proves that Mo Xuerong borrowed involved funds of RMB 13,040,000, repaid RMB 8,480,000, and surrendered ill-gotten gains of RMB 4,040,000, with RMB 520,000 still outstanding. The Guangzhou Intermediate Court dismissed the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department's lawsuit on the ground that it was not within the scope of criminal incidental civil actions, without conducting a substantive trial on its claim. Mo Xuerong's argument that the department was not a victim was untenable. Therefore, on April 17, 2012, it issued the criminal compensation reconsideration decision Gong Xing Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1, sustaining the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department's criminal compensation decision Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1.

The above facts are supported by: the criminal judgment (1999) Sui Zhong Fa Xing Jing Chu Zi No. 68, the criminal incidental civil ruling (1999) Sui Zhong Fa Xing Jing Chu Zi No. 68, the ruling (2001) Yue Gao Fa Xing Jing Zhong Zi No. 134, the civil mediation document (1999) Dong Fa Jing Chu Zi No. 361, the civil judgment (1999) Dong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 522, the civil judgment (1996) Sui Zhong Fa Jing Chu Zi No. 361, the civil judgment (1996) Sui Zhong Fa Jing Chu Zi No. 362, the civil judgment (1999) Sui Zhong Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 1748, the civil judgment (2001) Sui Zhong Fa Jing Zhong Zi No. 7, the civil judgment (1997) Yue Fa Jing Yi Shang Zi No. 248, the civil judgment (1997) Yue Fa Jing Yi Shang Zi No. 249, the civil judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 235; the criminal compensation decision Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1, the criminal compensation reconsideration decision Gong Xing Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1; the seizure list from the criminal case (1999) Sui Zhong Fa Xing Jing Chu Zi No. 68, bank fund flow vouchers, agreements on the investment, development, and transfer of the comprehensive commercial and residential building project at Fujin Road, Dongshan District, Guangzhou City, the joint venture agreement between Tianlong Company and Jinfeng Company, the receipt collected by Cao Huisong with Cao Huixiong's notation, Mo Xuerong's written statement, the interrogation record of Mo Xuerong, the inquiry records of Liu Jialin, Liu Jun, and Wu Chunyan, the interrogation records of Cao Huixiong and Zhao Leiyuan, and other case file evidence; the basic registration information of Tianlong Company, the enterprise computer-readable file registration information of Guangdong New Generation Computer City Co., Ltd., written certificates issued by the Guangzhou Municipal State Tax Bureau and Guangzhou Municipal Local Tax Bureau; the notice of assistance in deducting ill-gotten gains Yue Gong Han Zi [2012] No. 1242, the notice of assistance in deducting ill-gotten gains Yue Gong Han Zi [2012] No. 1243, the application for refund from the Guangdong Agricultural Bank Business Department, the credit voucher of China Agricultural Bank Guangzhou Taojin Sub-branch; and the written testimonies of Cao Huixiong and Lai Lili.

The Compensation Committee of this Court finds that the focus of this case is whether the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department should return the seized RMB 4,040,000 to Mo Xuerong. This focal issue can be broken down into three specific questions: First, whether the RMB 4,040,000 seized from Mo Xuerong by the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department constitutes ill-gotten gains in the case of Cao Huixiong's illegal borrowing; Second, whether the Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration determination that Tianlong Company borrowed RMB 2,100,000 from Huayin Company and Zhongyin Company through Xuanming Company and repaid principal of RMB 3,800,000, and that the interest and spreads of RMB 1,080,000 paid by Tianlong Company to Huayue Company were offset against the principal, is correct; Third, whether the Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration determination that the payments of RMB 6,934,562.5 to Jinfeng Company and RMB 849,000 to Cao Huixiong were not recognized as borrowed funds repaid by Mo Xuerong is correct.

Regarding the question of whether the RMB 4,040,000 seized from Mo Xuerong by the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department constitutes ill-gotten gains in Cao Huixiong's illegal borrowing case: Existing evidence proves that Tianlong Company was a private enterprise operated by Mo Xuerong. The Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department seized the ill-gotten gains of RMB 4,040,000 voluntarily surrendered by Mo Xuerong on five occasions due to the company's borrowing of funds, which was not improper. During the investigation of Cao Huixiong's suspected criminal case, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department seized the RMB 4,040,000 in ill-gotten gains surrendered by Mo Xuerong, issued receipts and a seizure list, and during the trial by the Compensation Committee of this Court, returned the involved seized and frozen funds to China Agricultural Bank Guangzhou Taojin Sub-branch, the actual victim that has borne the civil liability for repaying principal and interest. This action constituted an exercise of the public security organ's authority to recover and handle ill-gotten gains. The effective criminal judgment did not address the RMB 8,675,449.37 seized and frozen by the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department in its operative part, but it confirmed the recovery action in its factual findings and deducted the recovered funds when calculating actual losses. This factual finding is binding on this case. Therefore, both the public security organ's exercise of authority and the effective criminal judgment rendered by the people's court have confirmed that the RMB 4,040,000 seized from Mo Xuerong constituted ill-gotten gains in Cao Huixiong's illegal borrowing case. Mo Xuerong's claim that this RMB 4,040,000 was his lawful property is untenable.

Regarding the question of whether the Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration decision correctly determined that Tianlong Company borrowed RMB 2.1 million from Huayin Company and Zhongyin Company through Xuanming Company, repaid principal of RMB 3.8 million, and offset the RMB 1.08 million in interest and interest differentials paid by Tianlong Company to Huayue Company against the principal. The former fact has been confirmed by the effective criminal judgment in the case of Cao Huixiong's illegal lending, and is further supported by evidence in the case file, including the testimony of Liu Jialin, Wu Chunyan, and Mo Xuerong. In the process of fund lending, Huayin Company, Zhongyin Company, and Huayue Company established creditor-debtor relationships with Xuanming Company regarding the RMB 8.8 million lent by the former three companies, and Xuanming Company and Tianlong Company established a creditor-debtor relationship regarding the RMB 6.44 million borrowed by Xuanming Company. Tianlong Company's repayment of RMB 3.8 million in principal to Huayin Company and Zhongyin Company, the creditors of Xuanming Company, did not exceed the total amount of RMB 6.44 million that Tianlong Company borrowed from its creditor Xuanming Company. The Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration decision to offset the RMB 1.08 million in interest and interest differentials paid by Tianlong Company to Huayue Company against the principal is based on an effective civil mediation document. Mo Xuerong's claim that the Ministry of Public Security's above reconsideration determination is baseless and inconsistent with the facts is unfounded.

Regarding the question of whether the Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration decision correctly determined that the RMB 6,934,562.50 paid to Jinfeng Company and the RMB 849,000 paid to Cao Huixiong were not borrowed funds repaid by Mo Xuerong. The effective criminal judgment did not address whether these two payments were borrowed funds repaid by Tianlong Company. The fact that Tianlong Company paid RMB 6,934,562.50 to Jinfeng Company from the proceeds of the cooperative project transfer, of which RMB 5,787,500 was paid as principal and interest under the original investment agreement, and an additional RMB 1,147,062.50 was paid at Cao Huixiong's request, is supported by evidence in the case file of Cao Huixiong's illegal lending case, including multiple testimonies of Mo Xuerong, the agreement between Xiangxing Company and Jinfeng Company, the agreement between Tianlong Company and Jinfeng Company, and bank transfer vouchers. The fact that Cao Huixiong borrowed RMB 849,000 from Guangdong New Generation Computer City is supported by evidence in the case file of Cao Huixiong's illegal lending case, including a receipt endorsed by Cao Huixiong for collection by Cao Huisong, the confession of Zhao Leiyuan, and multiple testimonies of Mo Xuerong. The written testimony of Cao Huixiong and Lai Lili provided by Mo Xuerong to the Compensation Committee of this Court cannot overturn the facts established by the evidence in the previous criminal case file. The Ministry of Public Security's reconsideration decision not to recognize these two payments as borrowed funds repaid by Mo Xuerong is not improper.

In summary, the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department's seizure of RMB 4.04 million from Mo Xuerong during the investigation of the criminal case in which Cao Huixiong was suspected of committing a crime, and its return of that amount to the actual victims during the proceedings before the Compensation Committee of this Court, constitutes an official act of recovering and disposing of illicit money, which is lawful and well-founded. Mo Xuerong's request for the return of the RMB 4.04 million and its interest of RMB 4.2 million is untenable. The Criminal Compensation Decision (Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1) of the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department and the Criminal Compensation Reconsideration Decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1) of the Ministry of Public Security, which decided not to compensate Mo Xuerong, are correct and should be upheld. Pursuant to Article 18, Item (1), Article 25, Paragraph 2, and Article 29 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on State Compensation; Article 2 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the People's Republic of China on State Compensation; and Article 19, Item (1) and Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Procedures for the Compensation Committee of the People's Court to Hear State Compensation Cases, the Compensation Committee of this Court decides as follows:

The Criminal Compensation Decision (Yue Gong Xing Pei Zi [2012] No. 1) of the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department and the Criminal Compensation Reconsideration Decision (Gong Pei Fu Zi [2012] No. 1) of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China are upheld.

This decision is a legally effective decision.

September 23, 2013
